description: n512 B640 marquee shape: the blocked-Householder trailing apply (qr_panel_apply_fused) is 51% of runtime, a panel-sequential chain. Replace the well-conditioned subset's path with batched CholeskyQR2 (G=A^T A, Cholesky R, Q=A R^{-1}, repeated once for orthogonality), done entirely in BF16/TF32 tensor-core batched GEMMs with FP32 accumulate, then recover the compact Householder (H,tau) via orhr_col-style Householder reconstruction. Keep the per-matrix ill-conditioned geqrf fallback. Target turning the sequential panel chain into 3 big batched GEMMs the B200 tensor cores saturate.

Batched CholeskyQR2 (TF32 Gram, FP32 chol+TRSM, 2 passes) + orhr_col recon for n512 B>=120 good path. 22 test shapes PASS; diff_correctness guard FLAGGED 3 n512 shapes on mixed-case re-seeds: a few ill-conditioned matrices in mixed batches slip the good-gate (PD+colnorm) with factor residual scaled 21-25 vs gate 20. Need a tighter near-rank-deficient gate (R-diagonal conditioning).

Structural pre-gate (subsampled rankdef|nzfrac|collinear) routes ill-conditioned stress members to the exact mixed driver -> ALL guards PASS (diff_correctness CLEAN). But geomean REGRESSED to 2422.68 (baseline 1640): marquee n512 dense shape 3.15ms->37.1ms (12x), mixed 5.07->39.7ms. Batched torch.linalg.cholesky_ex + solve_triangular at B=640 n=512 dominate; PyTorch's batched potrf/trsm are far slower than the existing FP16 blocked kernel. Profiling next to replace the slow ops with cuBLAS/custom batched kernels.

BF16 Gram + blocked tensor-core TRSM (tri_solve_right_inv nb=128) for the two solves; TF32 R-matmul. Validates CLEAN. Shape 3 (n512 dense) 37.1->32.6ms, geomean 2371 (baseline 1640). TRSM swap helped marginally; dominant cost moved to batched potrf (cholesky_ex) and the orhr_col recon (panel_solve_fused ~2ms + diag_lu_reg + Schur GEMMs). Need to profile to confirm and attack the recon/potrf.

FP32 Gram (BF16 Gram made ALL 640 cond=2 dense non-PD -> whole-batch fallback). KEY NUMERICAL FINDING: cond=2 dense has cond(A) median 33661 / max 8.8e6, exceeding the FP32 CholeskyQR2 limit (~2900) for EVERY matrix; FP64-accurate Gram needed for all-PD (35/640 non-PD with FP32). Geomean 2407, shape3 35.2ms. Profile: dominant costs = batched potrf (~6.5ms over 2 passes) + orhr_col recon (~6ms), EACH ~2x the 3.15ms baseline, so this approach has a high floor at n512 B640.

1-pass CholeskyQR + tau-override: FAILS the factor-residual gate (scaled 21-65) on dense AND mixed re-seeds. The single FP32 Cholesky R1 is inaccurate for the high-cond matrices (cond(A)~1e6, cond(G)~1e13 >> FP32 cholesky range), so Q1 R1 != A -- the factor residual is NOT solve-bound when R itself is inaccurate. The 2nd CholeskyQR pass does real factor-residual work; 2-pass is mandatory. Reverting PASSES=2.

2-pass CholeskyQR2 (FP32 Gram) restored + validated CLEAN (all guards). Geomean 2406, shape3 35.26ms -- best VALID CholeskyQR2 config. Floor: FP32 SIMT Gram ~5.8ms + batched potrf ~6.5ms (2 passes) + orhr_col recon ~6ms + TRSM ~5ms. The recon still runs n4096-tuned defaults (FP64 panel-solve, register diag-LU, TF32 Schur). Next: enable the fast recon knobs (FP16 Schur/FP32 solve/warp-LU) for the n512 path since the tau-override owns orthogonality.

Fast recon knobs (FP16 Schur/FP32 panel-solve/warp-LU) enabled for n512 (tau-override owns orth -> only factor residual touched; validates CLEAN). Marginal: shape3 34.53ms, geomean 2408. The recon's B=640 cost is launch/sync-bound (panel-sequential blocked LU), not arithmetic, so precision levers barely help -- orhr_col recon floor is STRUCTURAL. CholeskyQR2+orhr_col at n512 B640 stays ~1.47x over the 1640 baseline; floor = SIMT/TF32 Gram + 2x batched potrf + panel-sequential orhr_col recon + blocked TRSM, the productive core alone (~8ms) exceeds the 3.15ms FP16-blocked baseline.

geqrf fallback for the small (~35/640) rejected high-cond subset: REGRESSES shape3 34.5->79.9ms (geomean 2582). torch.geqrf at n512 hits cuSOLVER's slow serial per-matrix loop; the FP16-batched mixed driver is the better fallback even for a tiny subset. Reverting to mixed-driver fallback (geomean 2408 is the best valid CholeskyQR2 number).

FINAL: revert fallback to mixed driver (trial 8 geqrf regressed). Identical to trial 7 -- 2-pass CholeskyQR2 (FP32 Gram) + fast-recon knobs + structural pre-gate. All guards PASS, geomean 2408.26, shape3 (n512 dense) 34.57ms vs baseline 3.15ms. Best VALID CholeskyQR2+orhr_col config. Profiled. Shapes 9/10 (rankdef/clustered) ~baseline (all-bad -> mixed driver); 3/7 regress (CholeskyQR2 floor).

Built and measured batched CholeskyQR2 + orhr_col Householder-reconstruction for the n512 B>=120 path (9 trials, branch HEAD 60eaa35). Best VALID config (trial 9, =trial 7): 2-pass CholeskyQR2 (FP32 Gram, tensor-core blocked TRSM tri_solve_right_inv nb=128, fast recon knobs FP16-Schur/FP32-solve/warp-LU enabled via the tau-override) + a subsampled structural pre-gate (rankdef|nzfrac|collinear) routing ill-conditioned members to the exact mixed driver. ALL guards PASS (diff_correctness/invariance/offgrid CLEAN). Geomean 2408 vs baseline 1640 (a ~1.47x REGRESSION); marquee shape3 (n512 dense) 34.57ms vs baseline 3.15ms; shape7 (mixed) 37.4 vs 5.07ms; shapes 9/10 (rankdef/clustered, all-bad -> mixed driver) ~baseline; all non-n512 shapes byte-unchanged.

WHY IT REGRESSES (profile-confirmed, profiles/.../brief-0-trial-9-*.nsys-rep): the existing FP16 blocked-Householder does shape3 in 3.15ms with 51% in one fused trailing kernel. CholeskyQR2+orhr_col's productive core ALONE exceeds that: FP32 Gram 5.8ms (SIMT sgemm -- FP32 can't use tensor cores), 2x batched potrf 6.5ms, blocked TRSM 5ms, and the orhr_col recon 6ms. The recon is a SECOND panel-sequential factorization (LU of Q-diag(D)) -- I traded the Householder panel chain for an LU panel chain of the same order, plus did ~2x the FLOPs (two Grams).

KEY NUMERICAL FINDING: the cond=2 dense scored shape is GENUINELY high-condition -- cond(A) median 33661, max 8.8e6 (measured via FP64 eig). Every matrix exceeds the FP32 CholeskyQR2 limit (~2900); BF16/TF32 Gram makes ALL 640 non-PD (whole-batch fallback = double work), FP32 Gram leaves 35/640 non-PD. The brief's 'BF16/TF32 Gram' is numerically insufficient for THIS shape; an FP64-accurate Gram+chol is needed for all-PD. 1-pass CholeskyQR FAILS the factor gate (scaled 21-65) -- R1 itself is inaccurate at cond(G)~1e13, so Q1 R1 != A; 2-pass is mandatory. The fast recon precision knobs barely moved it (recon is launch/sync-bound, not arithmetic).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (not yet tried, could lower the floor): (1) replace the FP32 SIMT Gram (5.8ms, the single biggest item) with an FP64-accurate TENSOR-CORE Gram -- the int-Ozaki INT8 path the n4096 arm already uses (exact INT32 -> all-PD, no fallback double-work) ported to batched n512, or cuBLAS BF16x9 emulation; (2) replace the 2x batched potrf (cuSOLVER potrfBatched ~6.5ms) with a custom batched tensor-core Cholesky; (3) attack the orhr_col recon (6ms) -- it runs n4096-tuned defaults at B=640 and is the structural floor; a batched/tensor-core recon or a cheaper Householder-reconstruction would be the highest-leverage win; (4) restructure to gate BEFORE pass-2+recon (gather the good subset first) to stop computing pass-2/recon on rejected matrices; (5) sweep _N512_TRSM_NB (only 128 tried). Even with the Gram and potrf made free, the recon+TRSM floor (~11ms) is ~3.5x the 3.15ms baseline, so this idea likely needs a fundamentally cheaper reconstruction to beat the FP16 blocked-Householder at this shape -- but I have NOT exhausted directions (2)/(3)/(4) and the int-Ozaki Gram, which are structural and could change the verdict.
